findings.claim: an open dense set can have dense complement
findings.proof: If U is open and dense and D\U were dense, then D\U is closed (complement of an open set) and dense, hence D\U = closure(D\U) = D, so U = empty. A nonempty open dense set therefore has a closed complement with empty interior (nowhere dense), never a dense complement.
findings.consequence: The stated reason for the open_dense_escape transfer failure is unsupported and must be replaced (the true reason is W3 and the strength inversion in ADJ-2).

findings.claim: the open-dense reading is weaker than the residual reading (WCC: 'the escape reading weakens the conjecture'; C0: 'open dense only strictly weaker')
findings.proof: An open dense U is comeager: comeager means containing a countable intersection of open dense sets, and U is the one-set intersection of itself. Hence an open-dense-generic claim entails the residual-generic claim. The converse fails: the irrationals in [0,1] are comeager with empty interior (W3), so no nonempty open subset of them exists. Therefore open_dense_escape is strictly STRONGER than residual_comeager.
findings.consequence: Fix the direction words, or state an explicit non-coverage ('holds only on') semantics. The two schemas must not disagree; the C0 row claiming no_transfer for open_dense_escape -> residual_comeager is the same inversion.

findings.claim: {pair: [open_dense_escape, residual_comeager], direction: no_transfer, witness: 'open dense does not imply comeager'}
findings.consequence: Use the paste-ready block in c0_transfer_failures_block.yaml. If the intent was that the notions are not equivalent, reverse the pair: residual_comeager -> open_dense_escape is the true no_transfer row, with W3.

findings.claim: a codimension statement neither implies nor is implied by residuality without further hypotheses
findings.verdict: half wrong under the closed-submanifold definition
findings.proof: With finite_codimension_complement defined as the complement of a CLOSED proper finite-codimension submanifold (codim >= 1), that complement is open and dense, hence comeager: the implication finite_codimension_complement -> residual_comeager holds definitionally. The converse fails via W3. The draft conflates this definitional transfer with the separate, genuinely unresolved question of whether the intended excluded set E_gen actually has finite codimension in D_w.
findings.consequence: Split the two questions in the schema text. If the owner defines the notion without closedness, ADJ-4 is withdrawn for that definition, but then the complement need not be open and open_dense_escape -> finite_codimension_complement must be re-examined too.

next_falsifier: If the owner declares an explicit 'only' (non-coverage) semantics, ADJ-2/ADJ-3 are withdrawn for that reading and the schemas must state it. If the owner defines finite_codimension_complement without closedness, ADJ-4 is withdrawn for that definition.
